newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, yen higher, marks weaken.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, yen higher, marks weaken.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, as cash mark/yen selling supported December yen, but kept mark futures on the defensive, traders and analysts said.
Light fund buying was noted in the $0.009020 area in December yen, but offers consistently cropped up in the yen futures pit everytime the December contract rose to the $0.009030 area, they said.
December's inability to scale through $0.009033, as traders were unwinding long mark/yen positions suggested the U.S. dollar would remain mired in a narrow trading range in the near term.
Likewise, December marks held well-above the three-week low of $0.6566, as the U.S. dollar found little upward momentum above the 1.5100 spot level, or about $0.6635.

"All these comments from G3 officials have put a floor on the dollar, but they have not given anyone a reason to buy dollars," one IMM futures floor trader said. December marks limited losses at $0.6626, which is roughly equivalent to the dollar/mark's high of 1.5117 spot.
Overnight, key Ministry of Finance official, Eisuke Sakakibara, said he welcomed the dollar's rise since April 1995, and said there was no change in forex policy.
This morning, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he welcomed the dollar's rise and would not mind if it rose a bit further.
Tietmeyer also said he believe central bank rates were currently appropriate, but added that the central bank would review the position every two weeks, as usual.

A U.S. Treasury aide reiterated on Wednesday that the U.S. administration remained committed to a strong U.S. dollar, but some analysts were concerned U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin did not make the statement.
"Traders want to hear it from the horses' mouth," one trader said.
Sterling futures remained higher after December set a contract high at $1.6656 on GLOBEX.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000038 at $0.009029, marks were down $0.0016 at $0.6638, Swiss francs were $0.0046 lower at $0.7863, sterling was up $0.0044 at $1.6634, Canadian dollars were down $0.0015 at $0.7499, Australian dollars were were up $0.0028 at $0.7898 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000650 at $0.123850. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
